inspiration.observed_pattern: Scalar conversion expressions explicitly transcode text to named MySQL character sets with CONVERT(expr USING charset).
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a label-encoding audit over fixed ASCII, accented, CJK, and NULL values. The report applies utf8mb4 and latin1 conversions and exposes character length while using newly authored rows and schema; the source literals and instructional examples are not copied.

fixture_notes: Rows cover ASCII, an accented label, CJK text, and SQL NULL. utf8mb4 preserves the authored text; latin1 conversion exercises MariaDB replacement behavior for characters outside latin1, while NULL remains NULL.
determinism_notes: Labels and IDs are fixed and ordered by the primary key; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE encoding_labels (label_id INT PRIMARY KEY, label_text VARCHAR(64) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 NULL)
INSERT INTO encoding_labels VALUES (11, 'alpha'), (22, 'café'), (33, '東京'), (44, NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT label_id, CONVERT(label_text USING utf8mb4) AS utf8_label, CONVERT(label_text USING latin1) AS latin1_label, CHAR_LENGTH(label_text) AS character_count FROM encoding_labels ORDER BY label_id

checks.sql: SELECT label_id, label_text FROM encoding_labels ORDER BY label_id
